title: Semantic consistency cohort eval and layerwise quant impact
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: build a repeatable, cohort-preserving evaluation harness that attributes degradation to specific quantization configurations (int8/int4; AWQ vs GPTQ) at layer and head granularity, and produce tuned acceptance boundaries used by the regression monitor and automated rollback flows. The focus is semantic consistency rather than token-level perplexity: measure whether outputs remain semantically equivalent for production prompt cohorts after quantization or config changes. This ticket implements the suite, runs a first sweep on two models (open-gpt-3b and redwood-instruct-7b), and delivers a proposed thresholding algorithm for alerts and rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible eval pipeline that accepts a config (model+quant profile) and outputs a per-cohort semantic-consistency report
Layerwise impact heatmaps (CSV + static image) that identify top-3 sensitive layers for a given profile
A proposed threshold algorithm with bootstrap-derived confidence intervals and cohort-aware correction documented in Confluence
Integration test that simulates an incoming deploy and triggers alert + optional automated rollback when thresholds are breached
Run artifacts (raw outputs, embedding diffs, human sample set) stored and linked to the ticket
experiments: Per-layer perturbation: applied AWQ per-layer rescale at layers [L4,L7,L20] and measured semantic loss across cohorts
AWQ vs GPTQ: matched effective bitwidth by adjusting G-params to compare equivalent compute profiles
Cohort partitioning: user-chat, search-snippet, code-generation. Ensured sample size >= 400 prompts per cohort
Stability metric: mean cosine similarity of sentence embeddings (text-embedding-ada-like) combined with a semantic edit-distance score from our unit-eval harness
Human evaluation: 200 AMT judgments on 'meaning preserved' (binary) for top-100 failing prompts across profiles
result_summary: Initial sweep shows semantic-consistency drops concentrated in two layer groups for open-gpt-3b with AWQ-int4: L6-L8 and L18-L19. Mean embedding cosine dropped 0.027 (baseline 0.941 -> 0.914) for the user-chat cohort; human binary preservation fell from 0.92 to 0.80 on failing prompts. GPTQ-int4 showed smaller average cosine drop (0.012) but more dispersed per-cohort variance. Bootstrap CI estimates indicate the observed drops are statistically significant (p < 0.01) for user-chat. The layerwise map correlates with attention-head sparsity in diagnostics.
design_decisions: Use embedding-cosine + binary human checks as primary signal rather than token-level perplexity to prioritize semantic preservation
Partition by cohort and keep cohort-aware thresholds to avoid false positives from cohort heterogeneity
Attribute impact to layers via targeted per-layer quant toggles rather than saliency-only heuristics
Thresholds set using bootstrap CIs with a conservative alpha=0.01 and a beta-binomial correction for small sample cohorts

notes: This ticket intentionally emphasizes semantic preservation as the primary guardrail for quantization rollouts. It complements token-level evals but serves as the production-facing signal for customer-impacting regressions. Keep all raw outputs immutable and linked to the run dashboard for auditability.
